title: Sensitivity invariant under Gaussian null changes
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ agree almost everywhere with respect to standard Gaussian measure: for almost every $z$, $z\in A$ if and only if $z\in B$. Then for every real $\theta$, their Gaussian rotation sensitivities are equal: $s_A(\theta)=s_B(\theta)$.
hypotheses_covered: $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ agree almost everywhere under standard Gaussian measure
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. For any sets $A,B\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\mathbf1_A=\mathbf1_B$ almost everywhere under $\gamma_n$, $s_A(t)=s_B(t)$ for every real $t$.
